title: Shilling Black-box Review-based Recommender Systems through Fake Review Generation

problem.claim: Review-Based Recommender Systems construct user and item representations from reviews, creating a potential vulnerability to shilling attacks.

gap.claim: The paper addresses the absence of a generation-based model for shilling attacks against Review-Based Recommender Systems.

contributions.claim: A generation-based shilling attack model is proposed for Review-Based Recommender Systems.
A fake review generator is learned through reinforcement learning to promote items by forcing prediction shifts after generated reviews are added.
Auxiliary rewards using pre-trained language models and aspect predictors are introduced to improve generated-review fluency and diversity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The framework reportedly attacks three kinds of Review-Based Recommender Systems on the Amazon corpus across three domains and on the Yelp corpus.
Human studies reportedly find that the generated reviews are fluent and informative.
Review-Based Recommender Systems with adversarial training are reportedly more robust to malicious reviews when equipped with Attack Review Generators.

narrative_sequence.summary: Review-Based Recommender Systems use reviews to construct user and item representations and help address cold-start problems.
Dependence on reviews may expose these systems to shilling attacks.
The paper proposes a generation-based attack model with a reinforcement-learning fake review generator and auxiliary rewards for fluency and diversity.
Experiments and human studies report attack success and fluent, informative generated reviews.
Adversarial training is reported to improve robustness against malicious reviews.

source_observation.claim: The attack generator optimizes prediction shifts while auxiliary rewards target review fluency and diversity.

interpretation.claim: Effective adversarial outputs may require jointly optimizing task impact and surface-level plausibility.

application.claim: When evaluating defenses against generated attacks, measure both system impact and the realism or quality of the generated content.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this joint optimization generalizes beyond the reported recommender-system settings.

source_observation.claim: Adversarial training is reported to make Review-Based Recommender Systems more robust to malicious reviews.

interpretation.claim: Training with adversarial examples may improve resilience to generated review attacks.

application.claim: Include generated malicious reviews in robustness-oriented recommender-system training or evaluation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the adversarial-training procedure or its transferability across systems and datasets.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the three kinds of Review-Based Recommender Systems evaluated.
The abstract does not report quantitative attack, fluency, diversity, or robustness results.
The abstract does not describe the reinforcement-learning algorithm, attack budget, or evaluation protocol.
